Mary Peltola vince in Alaska: i democratici salgono a 56 seggi al Senato USA

Secondo l'Associated Press, la democratica Mary Peltola ha battuto il senatore repubblicano Dan Sullivan con 144.302 voti contro 131.844, poco oltre il 50%. È il nono seggio strappato ai repubblicani in queste elezioni di metà mandato. Il Senato passa da 53-47 per i repubblicani a 56-44 per i democratici. La corsa è stata segnata dal caso di un secondo candidato di nome Dan Sullivan: Peltola nega ogni coinvolgimento, mentre secondo CNBC il Dipartimento di Giustizia ha aperto un'indagine penale.

Con un Senato all'opposizione, quanto cambierà il secondo mandato di Trump?

slide.titolo: Mary Peltola batte il repubblicano Dan Sullivan
slide.testo: L'ex deputata democratica vince il seggio dell'Alaska al Senato, secondo l'Associated Press. Sullivan era in carica da due mandati. È l'ultima corsa per il Senato delle elezioni di metà mandato 2026 a essere assegnata.
I repubblicani erano arrivati al voto con 53 seggi contro 47, ricorda l'ANSA. Ora i democratici ne hanno 56. Secondo CNBC, la maggioranza scatta da gennaio. Il partito ha conquistato anche la Camera.

Peltola ha superato di poco il 50% al primo turno, evitando il ballottaggio a preferenze. Lo spoglio è durato due settimane per i villaggi remoti e il voto per corrispondenza. Secondo DW, è il primo senatore democratico dell'Alaska da quasi 20 anni.

slide.titolo: Due candidati con lo stesso nome
slide.testo: Secondo un'inchiesta del New York Times, collaboratori di Peltola avrebbero reclutato un secondo Dan Sullivan per sottrarre voti al senatore. Peltola nega di sapere nulla. Quel candidato ha preso 4.760 voti: meno dello scarto finale.
Mi opporrò a chiunque per affrontare il sistema truccato di Washington e ottenere risultati per le famiglie lavoratrici dell'Alaska.

slide.titolo: La partita si sposta nei tribunali
slide.testo: Un giudice federale ha respinto la causa dell'amministrazione Trump per bloccare la certificazione. Secondo CNBC, il Dipartimento di Giustizia ha fatto ricorso e ha aperto un'indagine penale sulla candidatura del secondo Sullivan.

c.perche_ti_riguarda: Con 56 seggi su 100 i democratici potranno bloccare leggi e nomine di Trump e avviare indagini sulla sua amministrazione. Un Congresso ostile riduce i margini della Casa Bianca, anche nelle scelte che riguardano gli alleati come l'Italia.

sources.title: Democrat Mary Peltola unseats Republican and flips US Senate seat in tight race in Alaska
sources.text:
Democrats will control 56 seats in the 100-seat Senate which will give them the power to block legislation, launch broad investigations into Trump's administration and thwart his judicial and senior government appointments.
Democrat Mary Peltola flipped the US Senate seat in Alaska on Tuesday after a tight race that unseated Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan, according to the official ballot count.
With 50.12% of the vote, Peltola's win means the US Senate will have a 56-44 Democratic majority, clinching the chamber's last open race in a midterm election that crushed Republicans across the country and handed US President Donald Trump a firm rebuke of his second term.
"As our next United States Senator, I will stand up to anyone to take on the rigged system in DC and deliver results for Alaska's working families," Peltola said in a statement late on Tuesday.
"As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honour than having Alaskans' support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs and put Alaska first."
With far-flung rural voters in remote villages, the vote count in Alaska took two weeks to complete, but offered Peltola a strong mandate.
With 144,302 votes, Peltola beat Sullivan's 131,844 votes, even when combined with a second candidate named Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. who earned 4,760 votes.
Trump had called for another Republican candidate in the race, Gerald Heikes, to have his votes "immediately given" to Dan S. Sullivan, calling it the "fair solution."
Heikes won 6,105 votes in the race, but merging all the votes that Trump wanted to combine would still not have been enough to beat Peltola.
Dan Sullivan controversy
The Alaska Senate race had attracted national attention following a New York Times investigation revealing that aides to Peltola had recruited another man named Dan Sullivan to run for office with the goal of siphoning votes from the Republican incumbent.
"My opponent's campaign is literally focused on misleading Alaskans, lying and cheating," Senator Sullivan told reporters in Anchorage on election day.
Peltola has denied any knowledge of the alleged plot.
The fact that there were two candidates named Dan Sullivan had repeatedly drawn the ire of Trump, who said Democrats had used a "decoy" to siphon votes from the Republican candidate.
The Trump administration had gone so far as to ask the courts to block certification of the results if the incumbent Sullivan lost because of the potential mix-up.
The legal bid, which Trump has said he ordered personally, sparked alarm in political circles, but was dismissed by a federal judge ahead of the election.
However, US Attorney Michael Heyman claimed federal investigators were conducting both criminal and civil probes involving the Alaska Senate race.
Peltola's historic victory makes her one of the first two Native American women ever to be elected to the US Senate, where she will join Minnesota Senator-elect Peggy Flanagan.
Democrats will control 56 seats in the 100-seat Senate which will give them the power to block legislation, launch broad investigations into Trump's administration and thwart his judicial and senior government appointments.

sources.title: US Democrats flip Alaska Senate seat as Mary Peltola wins race
sources.text:
US Democrats flip Alaska Senate seat as Mary Peltola wins race
November 18, 2026
The Associated Press has declared Democrat Mary Peltola the winner of Alaska's Senate race after making it just over the 50% mark on first-rank votes.
Alaska was the last outstanding Senate race to be declared in the US midterm elections 2026 and makes it the ninth Republican-held Senate seat to be flipped.
The latest victory means the Democrats now hold a 56-44 majority in the US Senate. The 53-year-old is the first Democratic senator from the state in almost 20 years.
Peltola promises to deliver for 'Alaska's working families'
"As our next United States Senator, I will stand up to anyone to take on the rigged system in DC and deliver results for Alaska's working families," Peltola said in a statement.
"As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans' support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first," Peltola said.
Peltola beat Republican Dan Sullivan's 131,844 with 144,302 votes, the victory coming after an update in the vote count pushed her to 50.1% of the votes.
Peltola will now become one of the first two Native American women to ever be elected to the US Senate, where she will join Minnesota Senator-elect Peggy Flanagan.
Alaska's vast geography, remote rural communities and lengthy absentee ballot process contributed to a protracted count, with the Senate race taking over two weeks to produce a winner.
Vote siphon allegations
The Alaskan Senate race garnered a high degree of national interest after a New York Times report that aides to Peltola allegedly tried to use a second candidate named Dan J. Sullivan Jr, in an attempt to siphon votes from the Republican Dan Sullivan.
The Trump administration had approached the courts to block certifying the results in the event of there being a potential mix-up.
The legal bid was dismissed by a federal judge ahead of the election.
"My opponent's campaign is literally focused on misleading Alaskans, lying and cheating," Senator Sullivan told reporters in Anchorage on election day.
Peltola has denied any knowledge of an alleged plot. In any case, the margin of victory was greater than the number of votes won by the challenger Dan Sullivan, at just 4, 760.
The Democrats' majority had already been secured, allowing them to block legislation and begin investigations into members of President Donald Trump's administration, but the Alaska win will likely also have a morale impact on both sides.

sources.title: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate election
sources.text:
Democratic candidate Mary Peltola won the Alaska Senate election, capping a midterm cycle that already was one of the best for Democrats in more than a half-century, the Associated Press reported Tuesday evening.
Peltola defeated incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in a race that was surrounded by controversy over an independent candidate who shared his name.
Peltola had faced accusations that her campaign recruited ultra-longshot candidate Dan J. Sullivan to the race to confuse voters. The Justice Department filed a lawsuit seeking to delay certification of the election if the incumbent Sullivan lost in order to conduct an investigation into whether voter confusion tainted the outcome.
The Justice Department is appealing the dismissal of that civil suit. The department is also conducting a criminal investigation into the second Sullivan's decision to enter the race.
Peltola's victory gives Democrats a solid majority of 56 seats in the Senate beginning in January.
Democrats this cycle flipped nine Senate seats that are currently held by Republicans.
That outcome, which was not considered remotely likely at the beginning of the election, came as part of a massive Democratic wave this year, which saw the party also flip majority control of the House of Representatives by a decisive margin.
Alaska was the last Senate race to be called in the midterm elections. Peltola, a former House member, joins Senator-elect Peggy Flanagan as the first two Native American women elected to the Senate.
The race was called two weeks after Election Day, and six days after Peltola's fellow Democrat Scott Colom pulled off perhaps the most stunning upset of the 2026 cycle by defeating incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in the Mississippi Senate race.
As of 10:39 p.m. ET, Peltola had 50.1% of the vote, and Sullivan had 45.8%. Another Republican, Gerald Heikes, had 2.1% of the vote, while Daniel J. Sullivan had 1.6% of the vote.
If no candidate exceeded 50% of the vote, the election would have been decided through a ranked-choice method, in which the two bottom finishers would have been eliminated, and the second choices on the ballots of voters who selected them would be allocated to the remaining two candidates.
"From Juneau to Utqiagvik, the message from Alaskans is clear: the status quo in DC is not working for Alaska," Peltola said in a statement.
"Over the course of this campaign I've spoken with elders in tears about empty fish racks; families struggling to find housing they can afford; and parents in the Bush faced with the impossible choice of heating their homes or putting food on the table," Peltola said. "Today we take a monumental step forward in addressing those issues and putting Alaska first."
As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans' support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first," she said. "Thank you Alaska. Let's get to work."

slide.titolo: Colby attacca i "deep strike" di Kiev
slide.testo: Al quartier generale NATO in Belgio, il sottosegretario alla Difesa USA Elbridge Colby ha paragonato i raid ucraini in profondità in Russia a uno spettacolo. Secondo lui "non sono stati efficaci" per chiudere la guerra né per frenare le avanzate russe.

Colby cita gli attacchi a Wildberries, il più grande rivenditore online russo: colpire "infrastrutture civili" avrebbe rafforzato la determinazione russa. Kiev sostiene che i magazzini fornivano componenti militari. Wildberries e il Cremlino negano.
Secondo Colby, a ottobre le forze ucraine hanno conquistato più territorio della Russia per il secondo mese consecutivo. Gli attacchi a medio raggio con droni, ammette, sono stati "molto efficaci".
Criticare questi attacchi contro obiettivi militari strategici in Russia è una cosa piuttosto stupida, credo.
slide.autore: Boris Pistorius, ministro della Difesa tedesco

slide.testo: Il ministro della Difesa britannico Wes Streeting: "Non spetta a noi dire all'Ucraina come combattere la sua guerra". Secondo lui, i raid hanno contribuito a indebolire la macchina bellica di Putin, "guadagnando tempo e salvando vite".

slide.titolo: Colpito il ponte di Kerch, poi il vertice
slide.testo: Zelensky rivendica un'"operazione senza precedenti" con droni e missili sul ponte tra Russia e Crimea occupata, che è stato danneggiato. Mosca promette di ricostruirlo. Giovedì Trump, Putin e Xi si incontrano a Shenzhen, a margine dell'APEC.

c.perche_ti_riguarda: La divisione tra Washington ed Europa sulla strategia ucraina pesa su NATO e UE, di cui l'Italia fa parte. E i raid sulle raffinerie russe toccano l'energia: Trump li ha accusati di causare una carenza globale di gasolio.

His comments, delivered at a gathering of Ukraine's allies in Brussels, was flat out rejected by both Germany and the United Kingdom, who hit back at the Americans' suggestion. sources.title: Ukraine allies reject U.S. criticism of deep strikes inside Russia ahead of Trump-Putin-Xi summit
sources.text:
Germany and the U.K. have pushed back against U.S. criticism of Ukraine's deep strike campaign inside Russia, underscoring tensions between Washington and European allies over Kyiv's war strategy.
The clash comes ahead of a highly anticipated trilateral meeting on Thursday between U.S. President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, China.
Geopolitical flashpoints such as trade, artificial intelligence and nuclear weapons are expected to be a major focus of Trump, Putin and Xi's meeting, with external observers closely monitoring any discussion of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Speaking at NATO's headquarters in Belgium on Tuesday, U.S. Undersecretary of Defense Elbridge Colby likened Ukraine's deep strikes inside Russia to a spectacle, adding that they "have not been effective in driving an end to the war, nor do they contribute to blunting Russia's advances on the front line."
The Pentagon policy chief acknowledged Ukraine's mid-range strike campaign using novel drone technologies and tactics to deny Russian advances on the front line has proven "very effective."
He added that Ukraine's Armed Forces gained more territory than Russia for the second consecutive month in October.
However, Colby said Ukraine's deep strikes targeting "civilian infrastructure," citing Russia's biggest online retailer Wildberries, "have actually probably hardened the Russian public's resolve and the Kremlin's own willingness to escalate."
Kyiv has said that warehouses targeted by Ukrainian drones were involved in providing Russian forces with drone components, navigation equipment and other military components. Wildberries and the Kremlin have denied the company is involved in Russia's war in Ukraine.
Asked whether he shared Colby's position on Ukraine's deep strike campaign inside Russia, German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius said criticizing strikes designed to destroy strategic military and military-use targets in Russia "is quite a stupid thing, I think."
"Instead of criticizing that, we should rather criticize and talk about the terroristic strikes every night and every day on civil energy, water and heating infrastructure in Ukraine. This is kind of terrorism," Pistorius said at a news conference.
British Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting echoed those comments, saying it is "not for us to tell Ukraine how to fight their war."
He added: "There is no doubt in my mind that it has helped to degrade Putin's war machine, buying time and saving lives."
Kerch Bridge
Trump has previously called on Ukraine to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries and infrastructure used to produce and distribute diesel, saying the attacks were responsible for a global shortage.
Ukraine has stepped up its strikes on Russian oil facilities and logistics infrastructure in recent months, seeking to raise the cost of the war for Moscow after more than 4½ years of conflict.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Tuesday lauded an "unprecedented operation" targeting the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea in what marked a symbolic blow to the Kremlin's war effort.
A coordinated drone and missile strike on the bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian forces and is one of Putin's signature projects, damaged the crossing.
In response, Russia said the bridge would be restored and "will be even better than before."
